messages.content:
The record:
Write the postmortem for the incident below.

Alert: HighErrorRate on io-shop
What the alert said [AL1]: Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}
Alert raised: 2026-11-12T21:39:07Z {alert_raised}
Somebody was paged: an on-call incident was linked to this one. An alert rule fires; a person is paged.
The alert rule waits 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding before it fires. The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds {accounted_for} accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute {rule_evaluated_every}, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds {scraping_allowance} for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
Broken from 2026-11-12T21:33:00Z {began} (the onset, dated to its minute: a change came during that minute) to 2026-11-12T21:40:44Z {back_to_normal}, when Some Person reported it resolved [XW1] - their report is the end, as given. A report is not a hypothesis: do not test it against the rest of the record, and do not propose checking reports like it. Argus stopping at the report before it judged an action is the design: do not say it went wrong.
That is 7 minutes 44 seconds {duration}, and every impact figure below is measured over that stretch.
Argus held the incident for 1 minute 16 seconds {held}, until 2026-11-12T21:40:44Z {argus_stopped}. That is not how long the fault lasted, nor how long Argus went on working - leave it out of your answer.
The service's error rate over all its requests, before it began: 0.8% {errors_before}.
The same rate while it was broken: 28.6% {errors_while_broken}, peaking at 40.5% {errors_at_worst}.
Rise above baseline: 27.8% {errors_rise} of traffic failed that otherwise would not have.
The series behind the alert, `sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[1m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[1m]))` - its alert said "Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}" - which its alert rule evaluates and calls worse rising: 0.8% {series_before} before it began, 28.625% {series_while_broken} on average while it was broken, and 40.5% {series_at_worst} at its worst. Say what it measures in words, not by its query.
Customer loss: 5,194.52 USD {customer_loss} - how far the shop's takings over the incident fell short of the same hours whole weeks earlier, beyond how much those hours vary on their own.

What Argus did, in order:
  - [T1] 2026-11-12T21:39:28Z {T1.1} Argus: Received HighErrorRate on io-shop
  - [T2] 2026-11-12T21:39:45Z {T2.1} Argus: Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up
  - [T3] 2026-11-12T21:39:45Z {T3.1} Argus: Called in the Investigator Agent
  - [T4] 2026-11-12T21:39:45Z {T4.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's per-minute metrics, anchored on 21:39:07 {T4.2}
  - [T5] 2026-11-12T21:39:50Z {T5.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 360 {T5.2} minutes of metrics
  - [T6] 2026-11-12T21:39:52Z {T6.1} Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at 21:33 {T6.2}
  - [T7] 2026-11-12T21:39:52Z {T7.1} Investigator Agent: Recorded where the 3 {T7.2} replicas run - all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB
  - [T8] 2026-11-12T21:39:53Z {T8.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for production change events - deploys and releases, and flag changes from the flag provider's history, the 1 {T8.2} day 1 {T8.3} minute before Nov 12 21:34 {T8.4}
  - [T9] 2026-11-12T21:39:53Z {T9.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 1 {T9.2} production change
  - [T10] 2026-11-12T21:39:53Z {T10.1} Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 {T10.2} replicas run one revision, which the history does not name
  - [T11] 2026-11-12T21:39:54Z {T11.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's log lines, the 36 {T11.2} minutes 7 {T11.3} seconds before 21:39:07 {T11.4}
  - [T12] 2026-11-12T21:39:54Z {T12.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 123 {T12.2} log lines
  - [T13] 2026-11-12T21:39:56Z {T13.1} Investigator Agent: Formed 1 {T13.2} candidate cause, best first: C1
  - [T14] 2026-11-12T21:39:56Z {T14.1} Investigator Agent: Read every channel available
  - [T15] 2026-11-12T21:39:56Z {T15.1} Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 1 {T15.2} flag change by anyone but Argus, the 1 {T15.3} hour before 21:39:56 {T15.4}
  - [T16] 2026-11-12T21:39:57Z {T16.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATING to act on a candidate
  - [T17] 2026-11-12T21:39:58Z {T17.1} Argus: Called in the Mitigation Agent
  - [T18] 2026-11-12T21:40:03Z {T18.1} Mitigation Agent: Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1, moved from ON to OFF
  - [T19] 2026-11-12T21:40:09Z {T19.1} Mitigation Agent: Waiting to see whether the service is still at the incident's level, from 21:41 {T19.2} - up to 176s {T19.3}
  - [T20] 2026-11-12T21:40:09Z {T20.1} Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - no new minute read yet
  - [XW1] 2026-11-12T21:40:44Z {XW1.1} Some Person: Moved the incident to RESOLVED from PagerDuty - kept the flag off and paged the checkout team
  - [T21] 2026-11-12T21:40:50Z {T21.1} Mitigation Agent: Stopped before judging the action - a person ended the incident

Changes to production it read:
  - [P1] 2026-11-12T21:33:31Z {P1.1} flag-toggle monthly-spend-feature by admin: feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on
  - Deploys read, none came back.

Log lines it read, one per message:
  - [G7e5d] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 {G7e5d.1} evaluations - 30 {G7e5d.2} occurrences in 30 {G7e5d.3} minutes, 21:03–21:32 {G7e5d.4}
  - [Gad41] INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 10 {Gad41.1} occurrences in 27 {Gad41.2} minutes, 21:03–21:29 {Gad41.3}
  - [G46bc] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 35 {G46bc.1} occurrences in 29 {G46bc.2} minutes, 21:04–21:32 {G46bc.3}
  - [Gbac1] WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 27 {Gbac1.1} occurrences in 36 {Gbac1.2} minutes, 21:04–21:39 {Gbac1.3}; # was 0.50% {Gbac1.4} to 40.50% {Gbac1.5}, typically 1.50% {Gbac1.6}, highest at 21:36 {Gbac1.7}
  - [G971b] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 101 {G971b.1} / on 99 {G971b.2} - 200 {G971b.3} evaluations - 1 {G971b.4} occurrence in 1 {G971b.5} minute, 21:33 {G971b.6}
  - [G5309] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 {G5309.1} occurrences in 7 {G5309.2} minutes, 21:33–21:39 {G5309.3}
  - [Gce95] INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 {Gce95.1} evaluations - 6 {Gce95.2} occurrences in 6 {Gce95.3} minutes, 21:34–21:39 {Gce95.4}

Candidates it considered, in the Investigator's words - name them by their labels, but cite none; what they claim is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [C1] The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched from off to on at 2026-11-12T21:33:31Z {C1.1}. The newly enabled spend-summary path then raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 on account page requests, and the error rate rose from about 1% {C1.2} to 20-40% {C1.3}. [feature-flag-toggle, confidence 0.93 {C1.4}, tried, not judged]

Actions it took:
  - [M1] Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for [C1] (can be put back) - not judged, still in place

Action items the record already holds:
  - none
The document already states what set it off, in a section of its own: the change [P1] - suspected, not confirmed.

Cite evidence in causal_chain by its label. In a contributing factor's addressed_by, name the record's own action items that answer it, by their number; an item you propose names the factors it answers in its answers, by their labels.

Call submit_postmortem with your answer.

The document, by field:
root_cause: The spend-summary code that monthly-spend-feature turns on raises a ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 for some account page requests, and those requests fail with that error. The evidence does not show why the divisor is zero for those requests.
cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new monthly-spending feature sent account pages through new code that divided by zero for some shoppers, so their account pages failed.
still_at_risk: If anyone switches monthly-spend-feature back on before the spend-summary code is fixed, account pages could fail the same way again.
symptom: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
causal_chain 1: Shoppers' account page requests failed. (cites Gbac1, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 2: The requests failed with a ZeroDivisionError raised at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, starting in the minute the incident began. Before that minute, the only account-page failures logged were shoppers closing the connection. (cites G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G46bc, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 3: That code ran because admin switched the monthly-spend-feature flag on at {P1.1}. The flag read off on every evaluation before that minute, was split between off and on during that minute, and read on for every evaluation after it. (cites P1, under "Changes to production it read"; G7e5d, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G971b, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gce95, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 3 ruled_out 1: A deploy or a revision change: no deploy came back from the window that was read, the flag change was the only production change read back, and account pages rendered normally with the running revision in place before the onset. (cites T9, under "What Argus did, in order"; T10, under "What Argus did, in order"; Gad41, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; G7e5d, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 3 ruled_out 2: A different flag change: the flag provider's history showed only this one flag change by anyone other than Argus in the hour that was read. (cites T15, under "What Argus did, in order")
causal_chain 3 ruled_out 3: Shoppers closing their connections: these errors were logged while the service ran normally before the onset, and stopped being logged before it. (cites G46bc, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gad41, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
causal_chain 4: The code path behind the flag divides by a value that is zero for some account page requests, and those requests fail with the resulting error. (cites G5309, under "Log lines it read, one per message")
contributing_factors 1: The flag was switched from off for all traffic to on for all traffic within a single minute. No staged rollout, and no automatic check of the error rate tied to the flag change, was seen.
contributing_factors 1 had_it_been_otherwise: If the flag had been turned on for a small share of shoppers first, with an automatic error-rate check, only that share would have hit the failure, and the flag could have been turned back off before most account pages were affected.
contributing_factors 2: No test or pre-enablement check was seen that ran the spend-summary path with the flag on against account data that gives a zero divisor.
contributing_factors 2 had_it_been_otherwise: Such a test would have raised the ZeroDivisionError before the flag was switched on in production, and the flag would have stayed off until the code was fixed.
contributing_factors 3: No handling was seen that keeps an error in the spend-summary section from failing the whole account page.
contributing_factors 3 had_it_been_otherwise: Account pages could still have loaded without the spend summary, so shoppers would not have seen failed pages.
action_items 1: Fix the division at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 so that a zero divisor no longer raises an error.
action_items 2: Keep monthly-spend-feature off until the fix to src/io_shop/spend_summary.py is merged and deployed.
action_items 3: Roll out feature flags in production to a small share of traffic first, and turn the flag off automatically if the error rate rises after the change.
action_items 4: Require that code behind a feature flag is tested with the flag on, including edge-case account data such as zero values, before the flag can be switched on in production.
action_items 5: Make the account page still render, without the spend summary, when the spend-summary section raises an error.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {T5.1} or {duration}, are figures code writes in from the row they name. They are not judged.
  - Action items propose what to do; they make no claim about the record.
  - Whether something went well, went wrong or was lucky is a judgement. Only a fact it states is judged, and whether a went_wrong item is one its field excludes.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.

tools.name: judge_claims
